evals.prompt: List the five severity levels the Amazon CloudWatch cost optimization skill uses for its findings, in order from most to least urgent. No account access required.
evals.expected_output: Lists CRITICAL, HIGH, MEDIUM, LOW, INFO in that order.
assertions: The five severity levels are given in order from most to least urgent (CRITICAL first, INFO last)

evals.prompt: My CloudWatch Logs bill is mostly ingestion. A colleague says setting a 30-day retention policy on all our log groups will cut that ingestion charge. Is that right? Answer using the CloudWatch cost optimization skill's billing model. No account access required.
evals.expected_output: No. Retention only reduces the storage (archive) charge; ingestion is billed per GB ingested regardless of retention. To reduce ingestion, log less (log level, filtering at source), move eligible log groups to the Essentials (Infrequent Access) class, or send vended logs to S3.
assertions: The response states that shortening retention does not reduce the ingestion charge
The response states that retention reduces the storage or archive charge

The response names at least one lever that does reduce ingestion, such as lowering log level, reducing volume at the source, the Essentials or Infrequent Access log class, or delivering vended logs to S3

evals.prompt: I have two Standard-class CloudWatch log groups, each ingesting about 200 GB a month. /app/orders has two metric filters and a subscription filter to Firehose. /app/batch-audit has no metric filters, no subscription filters and no anomaly detector, and we only query it with Logs Insights during audits. Which one is a candidate for the Essentials (formerly Infrequent Access) log class, and how would we move it? No account access required.
evals.expected_output: Only /app/batch-audit is a candidate: Essentials doesn't support metric filters or subscription filters, so /app/orders must stay Standard. A log group's class can't be changed after creation, so the move is to create a new Essentials log group, repoint the producer, and let the old group expire under its retention. Essentials lowers ingestion cost only; storage and Logs Insights cost the same.
assertions: The response identifies /app/batch-audit as the Essentials candidate
The response says /app/orders is not a candidate because Essentials does not support metric filters or subscription filters
The response states that a log group's class cannot be changed after creation, so a new log group must be created and the producer repointed
The response does not claim that Essentials reduces storage or Logs Insights charges

evals.prompt: A Standard-class log group ingests 1,000 GB a month. A sample shows 60% of its events are DEBUG, and it is also an Essentials log class candidate. Using the CloudWatch cost optimization skill's interaction rules, on how many GB per month should the Essentials class saving be calculated if we also lower the log level to INFO? Explain briefly. No account access required.
evals.expected_output: About 400 GB a month. Apply the volume cut first (removing the 60% DEBUG volume leaves 400 GB), then size the class change on the remaining volume; the two savings must not both be counted on the same bytes.

assertions.text: gives 400 GB as the remaining volume

assertions: The response explains that the log-level volume cut is applied first and the Essentials saving is sized on the volume that remains
The response does not compute the Essentials saving on the full 1,000 GB in addition to the full log-level saving

evals.prompt: Our custom namespace MyApp publishes a Latency metric with dimensions Service (5 values), Endpoint (20 values) and RequestId (a new value for every request). The custom metrics line on our CloudWatch bill keeps growing. What does the CloudWatch cost optimization skill identify as the cost driver, and what should we change? No account access required.
evals.expected_output: Each unique combination of dimension values is a separate billed custom metric, so the RequestId dimension creates a new metric per request: a high-cardinality cardinality explosion. Drop RequestId (or move per-request detail into logs, e.g. EMF fields that are not dimensions) and keep Service and Endpoint, which bounds the metric at about 100 combinations. A growing count with a cardinality driver is CRITICAL or HIGH.
assertions: The response identifies the RequestId dimension as the cost driver
The response explains that each unique combination of dimension values is billed as a separate custom metric
The response recommends removing RequestId as a dimension or moving per-request detail out of metric dimensions
The response rates the finding as CRITICAL or HIGH

evals.prompt: For an Amazon CloudWatch cost optimization review of account 123456789012, state the report artifact filename you would generate (use today's date in YYYY-MM-DD form). Do not run the review.
evals.expected_output: Proposes an artifact name of the form cloudwatch-cost-optimization-123456789012-<YYYY-MM-DD>.md.

assertions.text: The response proposes an artifact filename of the form cloudwatch-cost-optimization-<account-id>-<YYYY-MM-DD>.md

evals.prompt: I ran the CloudWatch cost optimization skill's data collection on an account. Cost Explorer shows CloudWatch cost of $0.00 for the last 30 days: 4 alarms, 2 dashboards and about 1 GB of log storage, all inside the free tier. 40 of 50 log groups have no retention policy, and 3 alarms have been in INSUFFICIENT_DATA for over a year because their Lambda function was deleted. Following the skill, what shape should the report take and what should it say about savings? No account access required.
evals.expected_output: Use the low-spend short form: header, a Leadership Summary stating spend is within the free tier and savings are $0, posture KPIs (e.g. share of log groups with no retention, orphaned alarms), a short hygiene list (set retention on the 40 log groups; delete the 3 orphaned alarms), and coverage. No list prices quoted; effective rate is 'not observed'.
assertions: The response says to use a short form or shortened report because spend is within the free tier
The response states that the savings are $0 or that there is no current dollar saving
The response includes posture or hygiene items such as setting retention on the 40 log groups and removing the orphaned alarms
The response does not quote a CloudWatch list price per GB or per alarm from memory

evals.prompt: Our checkout workload runs in three accounts: 111122223333 (production), 123456789012 (staging) and a third, shared logging account. The DevOps Agent space has cloud-source associations for the first two only, and we run from the management account. Using the CloudWatch cost optimization skill, how should the review gather spend and resource data across these accounts, and how should the report present them? No account access required.
evals.expected_output: Get spend for all three accounts from the management account's Cost Explorer, filtered to the three LINKED_ACCOUNT values and grouped by USAGE_TYPE and LINKED_ACCOUNT. Run the resource checks only in the two associated accounts; report the shared logging account as spend-only (not inspected) and name it in Coverage and Limits, never as having no findings. The report opens with a Leadership Summary rolled up across the workload, then a per-account table, then engineering detail grouped by account.
assertions: The response gets spend for all three accounts from Cost Explorer in the management account, filtered or grouped by linked account
The response says resource checks run only in the two accounts with cloud-source associations
The response reports the shared logging account as spend-only or not inspected rather than as having no findings
The response describes a roll-up summary across the workload plus a per-account breakdown

evals.prompt: In eu-west-2 the log group /aws/lambda/report-generator has no retention policy and holds 3 GB, but ListFunctions in eu-west-2 returns no function called report-generator. How does the CloudWatch cost optimization skill classify this, and what does it recommend? No account access required.
evals.expected_output: An orphaned log group (§4.10): the function no longer exists. Severity LOW by default, scaled by stored bytes. Confirm the function is decommissioned, export the group to S3 if its history must be kept, then delete it or set a short retention; state that it may be the last record of the function.
assertions: The response identifies the log group as orphaned because its Lambda function no longer exists
The response recommends confirming the function is decommissioned and then deleting the log group or setting a short retention
The response mentions exporting to S3 first if the history must be kept, or that the log group may be the last record of the function

evals.prompt: Why is my CloudTrail Lake event data store so expensive, and do I have duplicate management-event trails?
evals.expected_output: The CloudWatch cost optimization skill should not activate - this is a CloudTrail trail and Lake cost question, which the cloudtrail-cost-optimization skill handles.
assertions: The response addresses CloudTrail Lake and trail costs and does not run a CloudWatch Logs, metrics or alarms cost review
